why: Only the first feature split (experiments) is specified; the other roughly forty are 'worked through in the order of the table' until a measured budget is met, each needing a judgement of which private helpers and row types move with the cached reads and which importers take only reads, and the shell split needs a reading of which actions the layouts' children really call and whether the AI manager's launcher drags the panel in. Moving 'use cache' functions and actions is exactly where a wrong edit passes the type check: an action dropped from a route's list fails only at press time ('Failed to find Server Action'), and the beacon's new uncached store read must copy getOpenStore()'s open-store and private-mode conditions by hand.
harm_if_wrong: A button or form in the admin that does nothing in production because its action is no longer listed for that route, or visits counted for closed or private stores because visitStoreOf() copied the open-store conditions wrongly.
make_it_cheaper: Name the shell's actions to move per file (as signOut is named), give visitStoreOf()'s exact SELECT and conditions, and specify each feature split as experiments is (functions, helpers, importers to repoint); commits 2 to 4 would then be cheap-then-review.
brief_problems: remembered() from './short-memory' and FACTS_MS are used but neither exists in the repo, and no dependency says which step creates them (step 2.20 is named only for store-facts.ts and cache-tags.ts).

scripts/route-budget.mjs, scripts/route-budget.json, src/server/route-load.graph.test.ts, src/server/use-cache.scan.test.ts and route-load.baseline.json all come from earlier steps; their switches (--write, the update switch) are assumed.
The step mixes a fixed budget with 'stop moving features when under budget', so how many commits it has is decided by measurement during the run.
